They could also pick up records meaning contact allergy, so drop them if you want only explicit terms.
- **M112 Infantile eczema and M113 Flexural eczema:** I included both because they sit in the M11 atopic dermatitis group.
- **M111-99 "Dermatitis/eczemas" and M111-97 "Dermatitis/eczemas NOS":** I left these out because they are too vague, even though they fall under M111. Add them if you want to match the Read hierarchy exactly.

**Left out**
- **Unspecified eczema codes** (e.g. M12z1 Eczema, Eczema NOS).
- **History and family history codes** (14F1 H/O: eczema, 12H1 FH: Eczema).
- **Other types of dermatitis:**
  - Within M11: napkin dermatitis (M110), infantile seborrhoeic dermatitis (M118), discoid eczema (M119) and asteatotic eczema (M11A).
  - Others: contact, seborrhoeic, varicose, constitutional/endogenous and pompholyx eczema.
- **Atopy that isn't eczema:** atopy itself, atopic asthma, atopic rhinitis, atopic conjunctivitis and keratoconjunctivitis, and atopic cataract.
- **Eczema herpeticum (A540):** this is an infection complicating eczema. Add it if you want complications counted.

**Judgement calls**
- **Included:** Eczema herpeticum, which nearly always happens on top of atopic eczema. Remove its two codes if you want a strictly specific list.
- **Included:** "Allergic eczema/dermatitis" and Besnier's prurigo, because they are treated as other names for atopic eczema.
- **Excluded:** Codes that don't say "atopic", such as M12z1 Eczema, Eczema NOS, Constitutional eczema and Endogenous eczema. Adding them would catch more patients but less precisely.
- **Excluded:** Two codes listed under "atopic dermatitis/eczema" with only generic names: M111-99 Dermatitis/eczemas and M111-97 Dermatitis/eczemas NOS.
- **Excluded:** Other conditions listed in the M11 section: M110 Napkin dermatitis, M118 Infantile seborrhoeic dermatitis and M11A Asteatotic eczema.
- **Excluded:** Contact, seborrhoeic, varicose and discoid eczema (when not labelled atopic) and pompholyx (hand and foot blistering eczema).
- **Excluded:** General atopy codes (Atopy, Atopic state), other atopic conditions (asthma, hay fever, eye conditions), and history, family history and referral codes. None of these shows the person has atopic eczema now.

- **Included:** Eczema herpeticum, which nearly always happens on top of atopic eczema. Remove its two codes if you want a strictly specific list.
- **Included:** "Allergic eczema/dermatitis" and Besnier's prurigo, because they are treated as other names for atopic eczema.
- **Excluded:** Codes that don't say "atopic", such as M12z1 Eczema, Eczema NOS, Constitutional eczema and Endogenous eczema. Adding them would catch more patients but less precisely.
- **Excluded:** Two codes listed under "atopic dermatitis/eczema" with only generic names: M111-99 Dermatitis/eczemas and M111-97 Dermatitis/eczemas NOS.
- **Excluded:** Other conditions listed in the M11 section: M110 Napkin dermatitis, M118 Infantile seborrhoeic dermatitis and M11A Asteatotic eczema.
- **Excluded:** Contact, seborrhoeic, varicose and discoid eczema (when not labelled atopic) and pompholyx (hand and foot blistering eczema).
- **Excluded:** General atopy codes (Atopy, Atopic state), other atopic conditions (asthma, hay fever, eye conditions), and history, family history and referral codes. None of these shows the person has atopic eczema now.
